why: LSP 3.17 textDocument/definition: a call resolves to the function defined with name() syntax. bash manual, SIMPLE COMMAND EXPANSION: the first word is the command name, looked up as a function first.

LSP 3.17 textDocument/definition: call inside another function resolves to the definition made with the function keyword and no parentheses. bash manual, SHELL GRAMMAR, Shell Function Definitions: both forms define a function.
bash manual, SHELL GRAMMAR, Shell Function Definitions: 'function name ()' is the combined form.
bash manual, FUNCTIONS: a definition takes effect when the command that defines it is executed, so the first call (line 3) runs the first definition and only that one.
bash manual, FUNCTIONS: the later definition replaces the earlier one; the second call runs only the second definition.
bash manual, FUNCTIONS: a function defined inside a function body is defined when that body runs; the call after it resolves to it.
bash manual, FUNCTIONS: function names are global: after outer has run, inner is callable at top level.
bash manual, SHELL BUILTIN COMMANDS, unset: 'unset -f' removes the function, so the last call has no definition.

bash manual, SIMPLE COMMAND EXPANSION: 'If the name does not contain slashes, the shell attempts to locate it. If there exists a shell function by that name, that function is invoked' before the builtin lookup.
bash manual, SHELL BUILTIN COMMANDS, builtin: runs the shell builtin and so bypasses a function of the same name.
bash manual, SHELL BUILTIN COMMANDS, command: runs the command 'suppressing the normal shell function lookup'.
bash manual, SHELL GRAMMAR, Compound Commands, if: only one branch runs, and which one depends on $FAST, so both definitions can be the one in effect.
bash manual, FUNCTIONS: a script that does not source another one cannot see its functions; the call resolves to the definition in the same file only.
bash manual, FUNCTIONS: same as the sibling file: the function of the same name in dup_a.sh is not in this shell.
bash manual, PARAMETERS: a variable is set by assignment; LIMIT has one assignment, so the read inside a function binds to it.
